requirement: A {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection` in a requirements input MUST continue to select requirements and named examples, excluding named definitions. Definitions referenced by selected texts MUST be captured as separate definition inputs, regardless of whether their names match the selection. Sharing a selection's matching name prefix alone MUST NOT make a definition a dependency.
rationale:
I found no gap against any of the three obligations.

**Obligation 1: a definition selection selects requirements and named examples, not named definitions.**
- `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[resolve]` (`Requirements` arm) skips `DefinitionKind::Term` and applies `definition_glob::matches`. It errors with "matches no requirement or example" when nothing matches. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[source_input]` also skips Terms and calls `resolve`, and `definition_inputs` reaches `source_input`.
- The CLI paths apply the same rule. `src/commands.rs#fn[info_markdown]` skips Terms and returns an error when no definition matches. `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_filtered]` reaches `status_markdown_with_github`, which checks `kind != Term && definition_glob::matches`.
- Tests:
  - `tests/definitions.rs#fn[selections_match_requirements_and_examples_but_never_named_definitions]` checks that `rules.*` selects `rules.ready` and `rules.case` but not `rules.used`. It checks that the exact name `rules.used` "matches no requirement or example". It runs `status` and `info` and asserts that `rules.used` is absent, and that `info rules.used` fails.
  - `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[requirements_reads_select_requirements_and_examples_but_not_definitions]` covers the `habeas` tool read.

**Obligation 2: definitions referenced by selected texts are captured as separate definition inputs, whether or not their names match.**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[definition_inputs]` calls `crate::terms::dependencies` and turns each result into a `Definition` input through `source_input`.
- `dependencies` calls `direct_references`, whose `Requirements` arm scans the body of each selected block for term references. `close_dependencies` then expands them to a fixed point. Names play no part, so a glossary term outside the glob is captured.
- Validation uses the same logic in `terms::validate_dependencies`. It requires exactly one definition input per required term.
- Test: `tests/definitions.rs#fn[globs_exclude_terms_but_capture_referenced_terms_outside_the_glob]` shows that the referenced `glossary.a` and `rules.used` are required. Dropping `rules.used` produces "rules.used, found 0".
- The authoring path (`definition_inputs`) has no test tagged for this requirement that feeds it a requirements input referencing an out-of-glob term. I did not count this as a gap, for two reasons. `definition_inputs` has no conditional of its own and delegates to the logic the validation test exercises. Authoring-side tests for `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` also cover it.

**Obligation 3: sharing a matching name prefix alone does not make a definition a dependency.**
- Dependencies come only from term references in the selected text, never from name matching, as shown in `direct_references` and `close_dependencies`.
- The same glob test above covers this. `rules.unrelated` shares the `rules.` prefix and is never required, and no error mentions it. A recorded selection whose matches include `rules.used` is reported as stale.

I found no unspecified extra behaviour in the `{impl}` items.
